ink.$description: Ink — Primary text, nav links, button labels, footer copy — the near-black (not pure) gives the page a slightly warmer, printed feel rather than a screen feel

paper.$description: Paper — Page canvas, input fills, button text on dark — the clean base against which warm off-white sections layer

atelier-white.$description: Atelier White — Light supporting surface for subtle backgrounds and section separation.

linen.$description: Linen — Deeper warm neutral for tertiary sections, input borders, subtle dividers — sits one step below Atelier White in the surface stack

stone.$description: Stone — Supporting neutral for secondary UI, dividers, and muted labels.

graphite.$description: Graphite — Supporting neutral for secondary UI, dividers, and muted labels. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

pebble.$description: Pebble — Input field borders, form field outlines, subtle structural dividers

smoke.$description: Smoke — Disabled button text and inactive state labels

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Long-form body text in editorial blocks where the slightly lighter tone than Ink reduces visual weight over long reads

pure-black.$description: Pure Black — SVG icon fills, logo lockup, strict black-tone elements where maximum contrast is required

margiela-sans.$description: All UI text, navigation, buttons, labels, captions. The custom sans is the structural voice of the system. Weights 375-500 handle body and nav; 600-700 appear in micro-labels at the upper edge. The extreme letter-spacing (0.067-0.125em) applied to the smaller sizes is a signature choice — uppercase micro-text at 8-12px breathes like engraved metalwork rather than digital UI. The narrow weight range (no display-weight condensation) means type never yells; hierarchy comes from tracking and size, not boldness.

margiela-serif.$description: The wordmark 'Maison Margiela Paris', editorial pull-quotes, product name captions, and serif body in select sections. Single weight (400) only, with hairline negative tracking (-0.004 to -0.002em) that makes the serif feel drawn rather than typeset. It appears sparingly — when it does, it signals a shift from UI to editorial register.
